- Model consistently overestimates early in the forecast horizon, especially in the first 5–10 days, then gradually underestimates later days.
- Forecasts tend to overshoot after sharp price spikes (e.g., 47–50+), then correct downward — model fails to capture the lagged mean reversion.
- Model exhibits persistent downward bias in the final 5–10 days of the 30-day forecast, especially when true prices show strong upward momentum.
- Model fails to adjust for sudden, large downward corrections (e.g., 47.00 → 35.94) — underestimates volatility and sharp drops.
- Model overreacts to recent high prices, producing overly optimistic forecasts when prices are near or above 45–50.
- Model underestimates the impact of seasonal or event-driven price drops (e.g., August → September transition) — fails to anticipate sharp downward corrections.
- Model shows poor calibration for the last 5–7 days of the forecast — often misses the true price floor or sudden reversal.
